Deep Dive
High-Level Overview
Orchard Robotics is a California-based agtech startup founded in 2022 that builds AI-powered camera systems and software to provide precise data on fruit crops, enabling farmers to optimize management decisions. Its core product, FruitScope, mounts on tractors or farm vehicles to capture high-resolution images analyzed by AI for metrics like fruit size, color, count, and health, feeding into Vault, a cloud-based system-of-record for farm operations. The company serves large-scale growers of apples, grapes, blueberries, cherries, almonds, pistachios, citrus, and strawberries, solving the critical lack of actionable data that forces multi-million-dollar decisions based on manual sampling and guesswork. With $22 million in oversubscribed Series A funding announced in September 2025 (bringing total capital to over $25 million), Orchard is doubling its team and opening a San Francisco office to fuel expansion, already deployed on major U.S. farms.
Origin Story
Orchard Robotics was founded in 2022 by Charlie Wu, a Thiel Fellow and Cornell University computer science dropout, inspired by his grandparents' apple farming in China. While at Cornell—a leading agriculture school—Wu connected with top fruit experts, uncovering how even the largest U.S. farms relied on imprecise manual inspections for critical decisions on labor, inputs, and management. He spun the company out of Cornell, initially raising $3.8 million in pre-seed and seed rounds led by Contrary and backed by General Catalyst, achieving early traction with leading apple and grape farms. This marked a pivotal shift from legacy farming challenges to scalable AI-driven precision, addressing long sales cycles and slow innovation in agtech.
Core Differentiators
Role in the Broader Tech Landscape
Orchard rides the precision agriculture wave, leveraging advances in machine learning, computer vision, and edge computing to make per-fruit data accessible beyond mega-farms—a breakthrough enabled only in the last five years. Timing aligns with escalating pressures on U.S. specialty crop growers: labor shortages, rising input costs, climate variability, and supply chain demands for yield predictability, where imprecise data bottlenecks multi-million decisions. Market forces like farm consolidation and tech adoption favor Orchard, positioning it to influence agtech by automating workflows and enabling sustainable practices—potentially expanding the $100B+ specialty crops market through data-driven efficiency. As an "AI farming company," it humanizes tech for an industry long left behind by innovation hurdles, fostering ecosystem-wide shifts toward profitable, resilient operations.
Quick Take & Future Outlook
Orchard Robotics is poised to dominate precision ag for orchards and vines, using its $25M+ war chest to scale FruitScope/Vault globally and build the full "farm OS" for end-to-end automation. Key trends like AI maturation, autonomous equipment integration, and sustainability mandates will accelerate adoption, potentially capturing workflows from scouting to sales. Its influence could evolve from data provider to indispensable platform, owning farm decisions amid competitors' consolidations—echoing its founding vision to secure America's food supply through tech that finally makes farming efficient and profitable.

Orchard Robotics Funding Announcement
Orchard Robotics has secured $22 million in an oversubscribed Series A round to expand its work in AI-driven farming technologies. The funding was led by Quiet Capital and Shine Capital, alongside continued participation from existing investors such as General Catalyst and Contrary. The company’s total funding now exceeds $25 million.
Additional investors include Nico Rosberg, Formula 1 World Champion, and Howard Lerman, founder of Yext and Roam. Michael Bloch, Partner at Quiet Capital, will join the board.
Technology and Products [...] Founder Charlie Wu said the company is addressing the data gap in agriculture: “Agriculture hasn’t fundamentally evolved in the last 20 years, despite dramatic increases in costs. Solving farming is a data problem, and data is the bedrock of every farming decision.”
Orchard Robotics’ Future Plans
With the new funding, Orchard Robotics plans to double its workforce by the end of the year and open a new office in San Francisco. The company aims to extend its services to additional growers across the U.S. and internationally, strengthening its role in precision agriculture.
#Funding#Orchard Robotics [...] Technology and Products
Orchard Robotics focuses on providing growers with more precise data for crop management. Its FruitScope Vision System is an AI-powered camera platform mounted on tractors or farm vehicles that captures and analyzes millions of images to assess plant health and growth.
The company also offers FruitScope Vault & OS, a system that tracks crop development and yield data, helping farmers manage inputs, labor, and harvesting decisions.
Current Deployment and Expansion
At present, Orchard Robotics’ technology is used by leading apple and grape farms in the United States. The company has recently expanded its applications to blueberries, cherries, almonds, pistachios, citrus, and strawberries.

Orchard Robotics CEO Talks Funding and Future Goals
The precision crop management company seeks to both expand into new crops as well as help growers better understand what’s going on with their farms through data.
Christina Herrick
technology
Precision crop management agtech company Orchard Robotics says it raised $22 million in a recent oversubscribed Series A funding round led by Quiet Capital and Shine Capital.
The company also says it has continued participation from General Catalyst, Contrary, Mythos, Valyrian, Ravelin and other investors such as F1 World Champion Nico Rosberg and Yext & Roam founder Howard Lerman.

Orchard Robotics CEO Talks Funding and Future Goals
The precision crop management company seeks to both expand into new crops as well as help growers better understand what’s going on with their farms through data.
Christina Herrick
technology
Precision crop management agtech company Orchard Robotics says it raised $22 million in a recent oversubscribed Series A funding round led by Quiet Capital and Shine Capital.
The company also says it has continued participation from General Catalyst, Contrary, Mythos, Valyrian, Ravelin and other investors such as F1 World Champion Nico Rosberg and Yext & Roam founder Howard Lerman.
With this funding round, Orchard Robotics founder Charlie Wu says he hopes to continue to expand on the data collected to better help growers in the future.
“That’s what we want to do, be able to give the most valuable information and the most integration of that information, so that growers can not only see everything they want to see and even more, but then also be able to use that data effectively in what they’re doing day to day,” he says.
Wu says he grew up in a farming family, and as he studied computer science at Cornell University, he realized growers have a strong need for good data.
“This lack of data is still a huge problem across the largest specialty crop farms,” he says.
Wu has expanded offices in Washington and California to better serve a growing number of crops including apples, grapes, blueberries and cherries as well as expanding into almonds, pistachios, citrus and strawberries.
“Our mission is just to help as many of our farmers as we can,” he says. “Scaling up, both the number of systems we have in the field, the number of farms we work on scaling up within our current farms, always just developing like new features for our growers. The thing about the camera system is that we’re capturing all of this data and we probably only scratch the surface — 10[%] or 20% of what we actually extract out of that data.”
Wu says since founding the company in 2022, he’s seen how valuable actionable data that the tractor-mounted FruitScope Vision System has been able to capture using artificial intelligence to analyze every visible detail of each tree, vine or plant.
“Our camera systems are able to basically capture anything the human eye can see,” he says. “What that means typically is like fruit counts, sizes, colors, disease detection on the fruit of the tree itself, measuring things like canopy area, fruit growth rate, getting yield estimates, size projection, measuring things like the tree trunk size, the height of the trees, inventories of where all the trees are. Anything that you would be able to see with the human eye, we can train our state-of-the-art AI models that run onboard the camera to be able to look for and basically get this data for growers accurately, but also at a large scale.”
And Wu says that, in turn, saves growers time and money and helps growers make better decisions on how to hire for harvest, how to market and sell the crop growing as well as save on labor and input costs with Orchard Robotics’ Vault and operating system.
“We can get it at a very granular level, down to the tree-by-tree level, but even having it at a general level, it is super valuable for our growers, because they’re able to make a lot better decisions based on that and end up with them becoming more efficient and then being more profitable overall,” he says.
